description: Flutter plugin for age verification, wrapping the Google Play Age Signals API on Android and Apple's DeclaredAgeRange API on iOS 26+.
rules: This plugin reports age signals the OS already holds. It is not identity verification, document scanning, or KYC, and it never returns a date of birth. Only an age range or bracket status is available.
Access the plugin through the singleton `AgeRangeSignals.instance`. There is no public constructor.

Import only `package:age_range_signals/age_range_signals.dart`. The `age_range_signals_method_channel` and `age_range_signals_platform_interface` libraries are federated-plugin plumbing, not application API.
Calling `AgeRangeSignalsPlatform.instance` directly skips the argument validation in the public wrapper. Subclass `AgeRangeSignalsPlatform` only to stub the plugin in tests.
Always `await AgeRangeSignals.instance.initialize(...)` before calling `checkAgeSignals()`. Skipping it throws `NotInitializedException`.

On iOS, `initialize(ageGates: [...])` is required. Apple accepts 1 to 3 gates and requires at least 2 years between consecutive gates, so `[13, 16, 18]` is valid and `[13, 14]` is rejected by the OS. On Android `ageGates` is optional and ignored.

`checkAgeSignals()` returns an `AgeSignalsResult` whose `status` is `verified`, `supervised`, `declined`, or `unknown`. Switch on all four. There is no `notAvailable` status: unavailability is thrown as `UnsupportedPlatformException`, not returned.

`ageLower` and `ageUpper` are nullable. They are populated on iOS only when the user consents to share, and on Android only for supervised users. Never assume they are non-null after a `verified` status.
`useMockData` and `mockData` are Android only, backed by Google's `FakeAgeSignalsManager`. They are silently ignored on iOS, which has no testing utility and requires a real iOS 26.2+ device.
Catch `AgeSignalsException` as the base type for all plugin errors. Each carries a `code` and a `details` string holding platform-specific diagnostics.
Exception subclasses, all suffixed `Exception`: ApiNotAvailable, UnsupportedPlatform, NotInitialized, MissingEntitlement, ApiError, PlayServices, NetworkError, UserNotSignedIn, UserCancelled.

`getRequiredRegulatoryFeatures()` needs iOS 26.4+ and an Xcode 26.4+ build. It returns an empty set on Android and throws `UnsupportedPlatformException` on older iOS, so an empty set always means no regulatory action is required, never unknown.

`showSignificantUpdateAcknowledgment()` throws `UnsupportedPlatformException` on Android and iOS below 26.4. Apple reports user dismissal with the same error as real unavailability, so `ApiNotAvailableException` is not proof the sheet never showed.
Platform floors: Android API 23+ with Google Play services; iOS 26.0 for the base API, 26.2 for regional eligibility, 26.4 for regulatory features.
iOS requires Apple's DeclaredAgeRange entitlement. A missing or unapproved entitlement throws `MissingEntitlementException`.

Google Play policy allows Age Signals data only for delivering age-appropriate experiences. Never route it to advertising, marketing, profiling, or analytics. That risks API termination and app suspension, so never log the result to an analytics SDK.
